Chief Complaint
Patient here with right hand and right ear pain, [STAFF]

History of Present Illness
Patient consented to use of documentation assistance. The patient is a [AGE] female with a history of right hand pain and finger locking, presenting for evaluation of right hand symptoms and right ear discomfort. Trigger finger and tenosynovitis of right hand The patient reports pain and locking in the index and third fingers of the right hand for a long time. Symptoms are aggravated by pulling tasks at work. She has previously used a splint in another setting and requests a work accommodation to avoid heavy pulling tasks. Colleagues assist her when possible. Impacted cerumen of right ear The patient expresses concern about cleanliness of the right ear and does not want it to get dirty.

Assessment/Plan
Patient is a [AGE] female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension presenting today for right hand pain and right ear symptoms. 1. Trigger finger of right hand (M65.30: Trigger finger, unspecified finger) - Right hand and finger pain with locking and difficulty attributed to trigger finger and tendinopathy, attributed to overuse and possible underlying arthritis; conservative management favored. - Provided splints for affected fingers and thumb to prevent bending and reduce locking and pain. - Referred to occupational therapy for further evaluation and management. - Provided hand exercises to perform at home. - Provided work accommodation guidance to limit pulling and heavy tasks as tolerated. Ordered: Ambulatory Referral 2. Tenosynovitis of finger (M65.949: Unspecified synovitis and tenosynovitis, unspecified hand) See plan under Trigger finger of right hand.
